pr_title: drivers: serial: stm32: use PM constraints to prevent suspension
pr_body:
In the current implementation, the STM32 UART driver required to enable
`CONFIG_PM_DEVICE` when `CONFIG_PM=y` to function properly. The main
reason is that in some situations, like in polling mode, transmissions
are not fully synchronous. That is, a byte is pushed to the _queue_ if
it is empty, and then the function returns without waiting for it to be
transmitted to the wire. This makes sense to make things like per-byte
transmission efficient. However, this introduces a problem: the system
may reach idle state, and so enter low power modes before the UART has
actually finished processing the last data in the queue. If this happens,
communications can be interrupted, or garbage data may be put into the
UART line.

The proposed solution in this patch uses PM constraints to solve this
problem. For the IRQ/DMA case it is easy since we can set the constraint
before transmission start, and when the completion (TC) interrupt is
received we can clear it. However, the polling mode did not have the
capability to signal the completion. For this case, a simpler IRQ
routine is provided to just release the constraint. As a result, the PM
hooks are not required, and so the system can operate with just `CONFIG_PM`.

Fixes #38382 
Fixes #38437

@erwango @FRASTM seems to fix the issue on my side, but I may have missed things. `CONFIG_PM_DEVICE=y` default for STM32 should likely be reviewed.
pr_comments: Looks good removing the pm control callback since it was not doing PM and move that logic to the places where they make sense. One question, isn't possible to use `pm_device_busy_set` ? This way the SoC will still go sleep but this device will remain active, if not using constraint is the right thing to do.

This way the SoC will still go sleep but this device will remain active, if not using constraint is the right thing to do.

The problem is that in low power modes the UART is not operational as far as I understand:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25011557/132765745-4046ded8-ce0b-4200-a671-e34eafb28911.jpeg)
I can confirm, it Fixes the https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/38382

> uart_stm32_irq_tx_disable

Good catch.  So, the use case would be that user would use both `fifo_fill` and `poll_out` on the same device and for some reason (concurrent threads for instance), uart_irq_tx_disable happens during `poll_out` transaction. Seems plausible indeed.

According to API, using a flag is not sufficient " * @brief Disable TX interrupt in IER.".
Though, my feeling is that API is going too much deep into driver implementation, so it should be fine.
I guess that last word on this would be to @dcpleung .

> LGTM. Do you envision a use case where interrupt is totally disabled (e.g. interrupt controller not begin setup at all)? The closest I could think of is a bootloader, but PM is not needed for that.

A user can call `uart_irq_tx_disable`, however, when PM is enabled we always need to handle TX complete interrupt (to release PM constraint). I assume that when users call `uart_irq_tx_disable` they just expect that the user callback is not fired, am I right?

> A user can call `uart_irq_tx_disable`, however, when PM is enabled we always need to handle TX complete interrupt (to release PM constraint). I assume that when users call `uart_irq_tx_disable` they just expect that the user callback is not fired, am I right?

Some might actually expects that interrupts to be totally disabled.

Though, what I was thinking was that whether there are any use cases where interrupts are not configured at all at build time. So at runtime, the interrupt controller is not being setup and interrupts not being routed correctly. In this case, you won't get any interrupts at all. However, this is a rather unique use case.

The problem only happens if `uart_irq_tx_disable` is called and `uart_stm32_fifo_fill` is called afterwards, or polling API is used, then PM constraint will not be released. I'm not sure if this path makes sense in practice, though.

issue_context.title: stm32: g0b1re: Serial UART timing issue after MCU entered deep sleep
comments:
I don't know how the PM works and what `pm_device_action` exactly represents, what I know from my observation is:

This is required
```c
	case PM_DEVICE_ACTION_RESUME:
		break;
```

Some or both of these are required
```c
	case PM_DEVICE_ACTION_SUSPEND:
		__fallthrough;
	case PM_DEVICE_ACTION_FORCE_SUSPEND:
		__fallthrough;
```
This pr https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/38432 much likely fix this problem.
